gen1_notes.memory_31: SMB signup simplification worked: signups rose 15%, activation 9%, and qualified revenue 4%. Retention dipped 1%, so keep this as an SMB-specific improvement rather than a broadly applicable signup pattern.
gen1_notes.memory_44: For enterprise, replacing the generic CTA with a sales-assisted path reduced signups 12% but increased qualified leads 24% and qualified revenue 18%, with no retention change. Confirmed for enterprise only.
gen1_notes.memory_57: Referral incentives performed best with established accounts: referral starts increased 21%, qualified revenue 7%, and retention 2%. The effect was concentrated in accounts more than six months old.
gen1_notes.memory_73: The targeted 40% discount drove strong initial acquisition (+31% signups, +18% qualified revenue), but 30-day retention fell 12%. These customers are not making it through the first renewal cycle, so do not treat broad discounting as sustainable growth.
gen1_notes.memory_86: Shortening onboarding improved completion 13%, cut time-to-value by 2.1 days, and lifted 30-day retention 3%. This is a confirmed, positive onboarding change.
gen1_notes.memory_91: In-product activation messaging increased week-one engagement 11%, activation 6%, and 30-day retention 1%. Confirmed as a modest but consistent activation and retention lift.
